hypothesis_h0: The effect is absent or small at the printed parameters; or conventional state-carrying controllers that contain no debt term (a hazard-learning filter; a leaky accumulator without settlement) produce a history effect of the same size, in which case the design does not discriminate decision debt from ordinary adaptive control.
hypothesis_h1: Re-implemented from the written equations with the printed parameters (lambda_eps 0.5, rho 0.10, hazard 0.05, accuracy 0.62, horizon 8, broadcast cost 6.0, capacities 1.0 / 0.35), the history effect (trials to escalation after resolved minus after deferred preparation) exceeds the matched controller's by at least 5 trials.
metric: history effect: trials to escalation after resolved preparation minus after deferred preparation (same test stream)
notes: Replicate = simulated participant; both conditions and all arms share the participant's streams, so the matched arm's effect is exactly zero by construction (an implementation check, as the manuscript says). Interpretation key: the claim is distinctive only if isrm_debt beats matched_no_debt AND the two no-debt state-carrying controls do not. Magnitude context from the theory audit: the printed 12.7 was produced with lambda_eps = 1.0 and frozen debt during the test; at the printed lambda_eps = 0.5 the auditor's re-derivation gives about 8.3 trials. Record per-condition escalation trials, censoring at 41 and carried debt as extras.
source_claim: With the parameters listed in Section 10.7 and 400 simulated participants per cell, the ISRM agent reaches escalation after 24.5 trials following resolved preparation and 11.7 after deferred preparation, a difference of 12.7 trials (d = 1.12). The matched controller shows a difference of exactly 0.0 trials, as it must. ... it is 19 trials at rho = 0.05 and 1.4 trials at rho = 0.80, and it is essentially flat in the number of deferred episodes once debt has reached equilibrium.
